On the surface, high school student Koyuki "Koyun" Hikawa seems unapproachable and terrifying to most other students. In reality, Koyun is just insecure and prone to overthinking due to her uncomfortable experiences in middle school. However, her chance encounter with two boys in school—Minato Amamiya and Youta Hino—sparks a change in her. Like her friend Miki Azumi, the boys are never afraid to approach Koyun and see her for who she really is.

Although Koyun starts spending more time with Miki, Minato, and Youta, she finds herself torn between her newfound bliss and her fear of getting too attached to others. Meanwhile, each of her friends quietly struggles with their own challenges. But as the new friend group continues to navigate high school together, Koyun and the others start to break out of their shells and enjoy their adolescence to the fullest.
anime.consensus_summary: The audience overwhelmingly praises Koori no Jouheki for its mature, realistic, and deeply relatable character writing and interpersonal dynamics, especially in its portrayal of drama and romance. While some viewers find the animation inconsistent and the season's ending abrupt, the consensus is that the show offers a refreshing and emotionally resonant experience that stands out in the genre.
pros: Realistic and relatable character development, particularly in portraying insecurities, social anxiety, and past traumas like bullying.
Genuine and well-executed interpersonal dynamics, including friendships and slow-burn romance, that feel authentic.
Strong writing that avoids unnatural drama, opting for believable communication and misunderstandings to drive the plot.
Excellent character depth for all main characters, not just the protagonist, contributing significantly to the narrative.
Mature and nuanced exploration of complex emotions and relationship dynamics, distinguishing it from typical rom-coms.
High-quality music, particularly the ending themes, which enhance emotional impact and atmosphere.
Visually pleasing art style and character designs that complement the story's tone.
cons: Inconsistent animation quality at times, especially when compared to other adaptations by the same author.
The season ending without full resolution, leaving plot points unresolved and requiring a second season for closure.
A perceived lack of high stakes or genuine tension in how character issues are resolved, sometimes feeling too easily overcome.
Some side characters could benefit from more development to feel less like background elements.
The portrayal of characters' self-awareness and ability to communicate their issues can feel unrealistic or overly idealized.
The love plot's pacing at the end of the season felt slow, with repetitive embarrassing situations.

anime.title: Li'l Miss Vampire Can't Suck Right
anime.genres: Comedy, Fantasy, School, Shounen, Urban Fantasy, Vampire
anime.synopsis:
In the city of Kashinokidai, where humans coexist with other beings, one individual stands out even among this diversity. Transfer student Luna Ishikawa, a vampire with a cool and mysterious aura, captivates her classmates and gains instant popularity.

Tatsuta Ootori, an otherwise unremarkable boy, believes that Ishikawa is far beyond his reach. However, when the two are paired for cleaning duty, Ootori discovers that beneath Luna's composed exterior lies an ironic secret. She cannot properly suck blood, forcing her to eat snacks to hide her weakness—but no amount ever seems to satisfy her.

Determined to help Luna master the very skill that defines her kind, Tatsuta offers himself as her practice partner. Through trial, error, and multiple bandages, their unassuming high school days take on a peculiar warmth—one where Luna no longer needs to act flawlessly and can simply be her natural, adorably awkward self.
anime.consensus_summary: The audience is divided on 'Chanto Suenai Kyuuketsuki-chan'. Some viewers found it to be a cute and enjoyable slice-of-life anime, while others criticized it for its clichéd plot, lack of depth, and the repetitive use of the chibi vampire trope. Overall, it seems to be a polarizing show with strong opinions on both sides, leaning towards mildly positive for fans of the genre.
pros: Generally wholesome and heartwarming interactions.
Enjoyable for fans of cute and lighthearted stories.
Some found the characters and their dynamics enjoyable.
cons: Plot is often considered clichéd and generic.
The 'chibi baby' vampire trope was seen as repetitive and off-putting by some.
Lack of depth in characters and world-building.

anime.title: Dragonite and the Special Delivery
anime.synopsis: Hana, a young girl from the Paldea region who admires the postman Dragonite and aspires to become an ace mail carrier, one day receives a letter with no address. Determined to find the sender, she embarks on a frantic search alongside her partner, Hogator. After running around town, she finally tracks down the sender—a boy named Rio. Upon hearing his story, Hana learns that Rio wrote the letter to celebrate his father's birthday, who is stationed alone in the Kanto region. However, the day of his father's birthday has already arrived...
anime.consensus_summary: The 'Kairyuu to Yuubinyasan' short is overwhelmingly praised for its emotional depth, beautiful animation, and effective world-building within a limited timeframe. While some critics found the inclusion of legendary Pokemon or the story's optimism somewhat forced, the general consensus is that it's a heartwarming and engaging experience, particularly for Pokemon fans. The short is generally considered a successful tribute to the franchise.
pros: Stunning animation quality by CoMix Wave Films
Emotionally resonant story with well-developed characters in a short runtime
Effective world-building showcasing Pokemon integration into everyday life
Excellent soundtrack that enhances emotional impact and excitement
cons: Inclusion of legendary Pokemon felt forced and unnecessary
Story felt rushed and needed more development to maximize impact
Hyper-optimism and positivity felt a bit heavy-handed

anime.title: Nmeneko
anime.synopsis: Follows the funny and amusing daily lives of two cats who want to live life doing only fun things.
anime.consensus_summary: Nmeneko is a charming slice-of-life anime that excels in its simplicity and realism. Audiences appreciate its relatable characters, pleasant art, and therapeutic "feel-good" nature. It's a straightforward show that delivers exactly what fans of the genre expect.
pros: Simple and realistic story
Relatable character relationships
Well-presented character personalities and expressions
Consistent character writing
Pleasant art style
Therapeutic effect
cons: Not much depth to the series
anime.thematic_vibe: Slice of Life, Comedy, Slice of Life

anime.title: The Shy Hero and the Assassin Princesses
anime.synopsis:
Toto has been dreaming about adventuring with other people for as long as he can remember. Despite his hero title, he still remains without allies due to his timid personality. Therefore, when three women: Ciel, Anemone, and Goa suddenly request to join him, Toto is overjoyed. Unbeknownst to him, they are all assassins assigned to eliminate him!

While Toto resolves to protect his would-be killers, the women fight over who can finish off the hero. As Toto remains oblivious of his new party members' true intentions and finds himself passing out every time he gets flustered, the four of them embark on their peculiar adventure into the greater world.
anime.consensus_summary: Audience sentiment is generally positive towards 'Kizetsu Yuusha to Ansatsu Hime', praising its comedic elements and character development, particularly for the female leads. However, some find the humor repetitive and the protagonist underdeveloped. Despite its flaws, many viewers found it an enjoyable and entertaining watch, with some hoping for a second season.
pros: Well-executed comedy with good timing.
Genuine character development, especially for the female leads.
Appealing art style and animation quality.
Enjoyable and simple plot suitable for lighthearted viewing.
cons: Repetitive humor, particularly the MC's fainting gag.
Underdeveloped protagonist with a lack of backstory and motivations.
Inconsistent pacing, with some arcs being weaker than others.
Generic fantasy worldbuilding and lack of depth in secondary characters.

anime.title: A Star Brighter Than the Sun
anime.synopsis:
Sae Iwata was never cute or dainty like the other girls, and due to her build and strength, she always felt the need to look after her delicate childhood friend and crush, Kouki Kamishiro. But as years passed, Kouki grew taller and more confident, which resulted in them drifting apart.

Toward the end of middle school, Sae reconnects with Kouki. Seeing that Kouki is still the sweet boy she once knew, she realizes that her dormant feelings for him have resurfaced. She tries her best to suppress her emotions—but it becomes even more difficult as, come high school, they end up in the same class. Ignoring her deepening feelings may seem like a fool's errand, but this boy that shines brighter than the sun may just prove to be her destiny.
anime.consensus_summary: Audience reception is mixed. Some appreciate the gentle romance, relatable insecurities, and classic shoujo elements. Others find the plot thin, characters one-dimensional, and the storyline repetitive, leading to frustration.
pros: Gentle and sweet romance.
Relatable portrayal of insecurities.
Wholesome chemistry between main characters.
Good supporting cast.
Female MC Perspective
Classic Shoujo elements are present and work well
cons: Thin and predictable plot.
One-dimensional characters.
Repetitive inner thoughts of the main character.
Lack of substantial development.
Awkward conversations and anxiety-induced monologues.
Bland storyline
Dense Protag
Misunderstandings

anime.title: Even a Replica Can Fall in Love
anime.synopsis: On days when Sunao is sick, or not feeling like going to school, she is called to take her place. She was born to this world when Sunao wished to have a substitute. No one knows that she exists, but she tries to do her best for Sunao whenever she is called. One day she talks with Sanada, one of her classmates. They become friends, but soon he notices that she is different from the original Sunao...he was the first one who did. She tells him to talk with her only when she has her hair half-up. Sanada does like she told him, and they enjoy their time together. As they become closer, she realizes that she has special feelings toward Sanada. But she doesn't know what will happen to her...if she, a replica, falls in love.
anime.consensus_summary: Audience reception for 'Replica datte, Koi wo Suru.' is divided, with strong appreciation for its unique premise and emotional core, but significant criticism regarding its execution and pacing. While many praise the character work and emotional impact, others feel the show failed to fully capitalize on its potential, resulting in a less intense and ultimately disappointing experience for some.
pros: The core concept of a replica falling in love is highly praised and considered unique and compelling.
The voice acting is consistently strong, with particular praise for the actress voicing both Nao and Sunao, successfully differentiating their personalities.
The adaptation successfully captures the emotional beats of the light novel and the pacing is considered excellent by some.
The ending, while abrupt for some, is seen as satisfying and poignant by others, especially with the introduction of a mature character towards the end.
Supporting cast contributions, especially in the latter half, are noted as adding depth to the themes.
cons: The execution fails to live up to the potential of the premise, often playing it too safe and lacking the intensity promised.
The direction is described as plain and could have elevated more scenes, particularly with sound direction.
The psychological elements are toned down compared to the source material, leaning more towards romance.
The middle portion of the series is seen as a stumble into slice-of-life, with characters and plot losing momentum.
The ending is criticized by some as abrupt, predictable, bland, and rushed, undermining character development and established themes.

anime.title: My Status as an Assassin Obviously Exceeds the Hero's
anime.romaji_title: Ansatsusha de Aru Ore no Status ga Yuusha yori mo Akiraka ni Tsuyoi no da ga
anime.synopsis: Oda Akira is the kind of guy who people forget is even there. His unassuming nature pays off, though, when his entire class is swept away to a fantasy world, and he slips easily into his new role as a silent assassin. Between his suspiciously high starting stats and too many details that don't fit, Akira is sure something is wrong. But digging into royal secrets is a dangerous game, and when Akira uncovers an evil scheme, he also makes a powerful enemy—the very king who brought him to this world! With the help of the elven spirit medium Amelia, can he find the power to set things right, and get his revenge?
anime.consensus_summary: Audience sentiment is mixed, with initial intrigue giving way to disappointment as the series progresses. While some appreciate the visual aspects and initial concept, many criticize the rushed pacing, weak character development, and unfulfilled potential. The series is seen as a generic isekai that fails to deliver on its early promise, leading to polarized opinions among viewers. Some found it enjoyable despite its flaws, while others strongly advise against watching.
pros: Visually appealing animation and character designs, especially in early episodes.
Reasonably well-established world-building compared to other isekai.
Interesting initial concept of an assassin protagonist in a fantasy world.
cons: Rushed pacing and incomplete plot development, especially after the first few episodes.
Weak and generic characterization; characters often rely on tired tropes.
Protagonist's internal conflict and moral dilemmas feel contrived and inconsistent.
Bait-and-switch from a darker action story to a generic isekai romance.
Overpowered protagonist with no real power progression, leading to a lack of tension.

anime.title: The Cat and the Dragon
anime.synopsis: An orphan since hatched, a lone dragon named "Uncle Wings" is taken in by a family of magic-wielding cats and raised as one of their own. As Uncle Wings grows, he becomes the cats' protector, determined to keep them safe from humans. But as he watches the cats connect with humans using their magic, Uncle Wings slowly starts to warm up to humans in this heartfelt, bittersweet tale.
anime.consensus_summary: Audiences are generally charmed by Neko to Ryuu's cozy, heartwarming slice-of-life fantasy, praising its beautiful animation and emotional depth in specific episodes. However, there's a notable split regarding its episodic structure and pacing; while some find it a relaxing and engaging anthology, others critique the lack of a central plot, limited dragon focus, and potential for boredom.
pros: Beautiful animation and art style, often described as Ghibli-esque.
Relaxing and cozy atmosphere, providing stress relief and comfort.
Strong emotional resonance in certain episodes, particularly episode 11.
Well-developed characters with distinct personalities, despite the episodic nature.
Unique and heartwarming premise of a dragon raised by cats, leading to a protective nature.
Positive portrayal of motherhood and chosen family dynamics.
Engaging episodic storytelling that keeps viewers interested with varied mini-stories.
cons: The dragon protagonist, while central to the premise, often has limited screen time and character development.
The episodic, anthology-like structure can lead to a lack of a cohesive overarching plot and make it difficult to form deep attachments to characters.
Some viewers found the show boring or lacking in significant plot or character development, especially those expecting more action or a traditional narrative.
The description and initial premise can be misleading, as the focus shifts heavily to the cats and their stories rather than the dragon.
While the animation is praised, some felt the world-building and story ultimately built to nothing substantial.

anime.title: Ninja vs. Gokudo
anime.genres: Action, Adult Cast, Martial Arts, Organized Crime
anime.synopsis:
Since ancient times, the ninja and the yakuza have been at war, spilling blood around the world as empires rise and fall. So when, in the modern age, Shinoha, a ninja, meets Kiwami, a gangster following the path of the yakuza—the gokudo—and discovers they have common interests, the obvious assumption is that nothing good can come of it. But can it be that one burgeoning bromance will shake up a 300-year grudge?

Who will win the struggle for real ultimate power?
anime.consensus_summary: The anime is a 'love it or hate it' experience, with some viewers appreciating its over-the-top action and bromance, while others are critical of its animation quality and pacing. The show has a cult following due to its unique blend of ninja and yakuza themes. Despite its flaws, some find it enjoyable as a brainless action series.
pros: Unique story and plot with unexpected directions.
Bromance between main characters is a highlight.
Action sequences are entertaining for fans of the genre.
cons: Overuse of villain backstories.
Inconsistent animation quality, particularly from Studio Deen.
Pacing issues, with certain arcs feeling rushed.

anime.title: Touring After the Apocalypse
anime.genres: Adventure, Sci-Fi, Seinen, Slice of Life
anime.synopsis: All alone after the end of days, two girls bike through the empty ruins of Japan—and they're not about to let the collapse of civilization get in the way of sightseeing! Even when the world ends, their journey goes on.
anime.consensus_summary: The audience generally appreciates Shuumatsu Touring for its unique take on the post-apocalyptic genre, focusing on the beauty and mystery of a world reclaimed by nature. The characters and their journey are enjoyable, but some find the lack of definitive answers about the world's past and inconsistent animation quality to be drawbacks. Overall, the show evokes a sense of peaceful melancholy and intrigue, with a segment of viewers finding it to be an emotional and thought-provoking experience.
pros: Beautiful and immersive background art that makes the environment a character.
Exploration of post-apocalyptic themes with a focus on the beauty and mystery of the world.
Likeable characters with a fun dynamic.
Intriguing world building with hints of the past and the cause of the apocalypse.
cons: Animation quality is not always consistent.
Some viewers may find the slow pace and lack of answers frustrating.
May not appeal to viewers expecting a more action-oriented post-apocalyptic story.
Comparisons to Girls' Last Tour may lead to unmet expectations.
anime.thematic_vibe: Post-Apocalyptic Solace, Melancholic Beauty, Existential Mystery

anime.title: Himitsu no AiPri: Ring-hen
anime.synopsis: Second season of Himitsu no AiPri.
anime.consensus_summary: The second season is considered a step down from the first, with a bloated cast and an uninteresting main plot detracting from the core emotional elements. The introduction of new characters initially shows promise but ultimately fails to deliver depth and integration into the story. The ending lacks emotional resonance, leaving viewers disappointed with the overall narrative.
pros: Introduction of new characters has the same energy and writing as the first season.
Early episodes capture the human and personal feel of the first season.
cons: New characters lack depth and are not well-integrated into the overarching story.
Princess Ring plotline is uninteresting and fails to carry the main plot.
Cast is too large, diluting the focus on core relationships and emotional depth.
Interesting plotlines are weakened by the bloated cast and Ring plot.
Ending lacks emotional impact.

anime.title: Beastars Final Season Part 2
anime.synopsis: Second part of Beastars Final Season.
anime.consensus_summary: Audience reception for Beastars Final Season Part 2 is deeply divided, with a significant portion expressing strong disappointment with the rushed and nonsensical conclusion, while a smaller, vocal group found it thought-provoking and a satisfactory, albeit imperfect, finale. The animation and world-building are still praised, but the narrative quality, particularly in the latter half, is heavily criticized for plot holes, dropped threads, and uncharacteristic character decisions.
pros: Strong worldbuilding and attention to detail remain
Cinematography and animation quality are consistently high
Some bright spots of characterization and thematic intrigue, particularly regarding Melon
Louis and Legoshi's relationship development to a more mature brotherhood is highlighted
The ending, while rushed for some, is seen by others as thought-provoking and a difficult balance of realism and hope
Voice actors are well-chosen and deliver strong performances
Some changes from the manga were seen as improvements, offering more screen time to characters like Haru and Juno
cons: The ending is widely criticized as rushed, nonsensical, and anticlimactic
Many plot points come out of nowhere or are resolved through convenient exposition dumps
Characters, particularly Legoshi, make uncharacteristic and convenient mistakes to drive the plot
Several plot threads are introduced but not adequately resolved or are cut entirely
The adaptation cuts significant content from the manga, weakening character arcs and plot points
Worldbuilding rules are sometimes broken to serve the plot
The writing quality plummets in the latter half, with plot holes and nonsensical situations
New characters introduced in the finale are underdeveloped and uninteresting
The overall pacing is too fast, especially in the final episodes, leading to a lack of emotional weight
The adaptation worsens existing issues from the manga's ending
The opening sequence is considered lackluster compared to previous seasons

anime.title: Jack-of-All-Trades, Party of None
anime.synopsis:
"Orhun Dura, today will be your last day in the party."

Orhun, once a skilled Swordsman, had adapted to the role of Enchanter to fill a crucial gap in the Hero Party. However, one day, the party leader abruptly dismisses him, claiming his skills are lacking. Branded a "weakling" and a "jack of all trades, master of none," by his former comrades, Orhun is cast out without a second thought.

Determined to start anew, he returns to adventuring—this time as a Swordsman, the role he originally excelled in. But his time as an Enchanter was far from wasted. The experience, knowledge, and countless original spells he developed in the Hero Party have forged him into a warrior unlike any other. Now, armed with an unconventional set of skills, Orhun is ready to carve his own path—one that will prove his true strength to the world.
anime.consensus_summary: Audience sentiment is mixed, with many finding the show generic and falling into overused tropes, particularly in the 'kicked from the hero party' subgenre. Some viewers appreciated the world-building and potential shown in the later episodes, finding it a guilty pleasure. However, significant criticisms include poor animation, weak characters, and a disappointing second half, resulting in a divisive reception.
pros: Decent world-building and plot intrigue, especially in the second half
Some find it enjoyable as a guilty pleasure, mindless fun
CGI is decent compared to similar shows
Potential for a good second season if it gets one
Interesting concepts, story is deeper than usual trope
cons: Generic story and characters, relies too much on overused tropes
Story quality drops significantly in the second half
Poor animation with clunky CGI
Lackluster fight scenes with too much talking and passive enemies
Side characters are forgettable and underdeveloped
Plot holes and unsatisfying ending
MC has multiple OP abilities which are not explained

anime.title: Tojima Wants to Be a Kamen Rider
anime.romaji_title: Toujima Tanzaburou wa Kamen Rider ni Naritai
anime.genres: Action, Adult Cast, Comedy, Seinen, Super Power
anime.synopsis:
Tanzaburou Toujima has spent his entire life chasing a dream: to become Kamen Rider. Now, at 40, reality has nearly caught up with him, and he's on the verge of letting go of his childhood fantasy.

That is, until he gets caught up in a crime wave led by the "Fake Shocker" gang—turning his long-time dream into something far more dangerous.

What starts as a pretend hero's journey quickly becomes something real. The ultimate Kamen Rider fantasy is about to begin!
anime.consensus_summary: The show is a highly enjoyable and action-packed comedy, especially for fans of Kamen Rider. Viewers appreciate the passion and dedication poured into the series, praising its characters, music, and action. However, some criticisms include shallow storytelling, pacing issues, and potential misogynistic elements. Overall, audiences are thrilled with the experience and desire a second season.
pros: The show is a love letter to Kamen Rider and tokusatsu genre, filled with references and homages that appeal to fans.
Characters are over-the-top but have distinct personalities and arcs, making them engaging and likeable.
The music by TeddyLoid is a highlight, with memorable themes and sound design that intensifies action scenes.
Action sequences are well-directed and feel like brutal slugfests, despite budget limitations.
cons: Story can be shallow at times, with simple characterization and a basic plot.
Pacing issues, particularly in the middle section, where training arcs drag on.
Some reviewers find the female characters are sexualized and sometimes mistreated, leading to misogyny claims.
Animation can be inconsistent due to budget constraints, although the style often fits the old-school aesthetic.

anime.title: Black Torch
anime.synopsis:
Capable of communicating with animals, Jirou Azuma, a troublesome 17-year-old high school student, is constantly scolded by his grandfather for fighting humans that harm his winged and four-legged friends. However, after Jirou saves a black cat named Ragou from certain death, his carefree existence soon comes to an end.

Unbeknownst to Jirou, Ragou is no ordinary cat but a mononoke, a magical creature of immense power. While trying to protect Ragou from another mononoke, Jirou is easily defeated and left for dead. In a dramatic turn of events, Ragou decides to pay off his debt to the dying young man, making Jirou a rare human-mononoke hybrid that easily overpowers his aggressor.

Unfortunately, Jirou is now sought by both Ragou's kin who want to use the latter's powers, and the Bureau of Espionage, a secret governmental organization protecting civilians against hostile mononoke. Forcibly enlisted by the Bureau of Espionage's Ryousuke Shiba, Jirou must prove his worth in a new anti-mononoke task force, lest he be killed as a menace himself.
anime.consensus_summary: Audience opinion is sharply divided, with praise for animation and sound clashing with widespread criticism of its unoriginality, shallow characters, and inconsistent writing. While some find it a fun, albeit stereotypical, action romp, many feel it fails to stand out and relies too heavily on tropes and fan service.
pros: Animation and visuals are solid, with good character designs and color palettes.
Action sequences are well-executed and visually appealing.
The soundtrack and music, including OP/ED, are surprisingly good.
The dynamic between the protagonist and Ragou is a redeeming aspect.
cons: Overly reliant on clichés and derivative of other shonen series like Bleach.
Inconsistent writing, abandonment of established lore/abilities, and plot convenience over logic.
Shallow and underdeveloped characters with predictable archetypes.
Excessive and unnecessary fan service, particularly focusing on female characters' bodies.
Rushed pacing, especially in the latter half, leading to underdeveloped plot points and character arcs.
Generic and forgettable story that lacks originality and impact.

anime.title: A Gatherer's Adventure in Isekai
anime.synopsis:
Living in constant monotone, Takeru Kamishiro longs for a change in his life. His wish is seemingly granted when a god reincarnates him in Madeus, a world trapped in a cycle of collapse. Hoping that Takeru's presence might finally save the world, the god grants him invaluable gifts: a new body with potent magic, a bottomless bag, and a skill that allows him to locate and appraise materials and treasures.

Thrust into a new adventure, Takeru begins his new life exploring freely and collecting valuables to sell. However, as he journeys alongside a newly hatched dragon, his quiet actions start to send ripples across the world—subtly changing its future toward the unseen.
anime.consensus_summary: The overall audience mood is negative, with many finding the anime to be a generic and boring addition to the isekai genre. While some appreciate its relaxing nature and the cute baby dragon, the majority criticize its uninspired story, bland characters, and poor execution.  Viewers generally agree it's a skippable title given the wealth of better anime available.
pros: Some viewers find it a relaxing and easy watch.
The baby dragon is considered cute and a highlight for some.
A few supporting characters are likeable and have some development.
cons: The story is generic and predictable, relying heavily on isekai cliches.
The main character is bland, unlikeable, and often hypocritical.
The gathering aspect is shallow and quickly abandoned.
Pacing issues and lack of plot depth make it hard to stay invested.
Animation and character design are mediocre or subpar.
The power system is poorly defined, and the MC is overpowered with no real challenges.

anime.title: Style of Hiroshi Nohara's Lunch
anime.romaji_title: Nohara Hiroshi: Hiru Meshi no Ryuugi
anime.synopsis:
This series follows Hiroshi Nohara's ultimate lunchtime philosophy, as he carefully selects and enjoys his midday meals within the constraints of a limited budget and break time.

But it's not just about savoring food—Hiroshi delves into cooking trivia, preparation methods, and the everyday dilemmas of a salaryman. From debating whether to treat his juniors to lunch, to finding quick meals between sales meetings, and even venting about his boss, the series is packed with relatable moments for working professionals.
anime.consensus_summary: The audience consensus is overwhelmingly positive, particularly among fans of Crayon Shinchan and slice-of-life anime. Viewers find the show comforting, funny, and relatable, appreciating its focus on food and its uplifting message. The animation and music are also well-received, contributing to the overall positive experience.
pros: Enjoyable slice of life and food anime combination.
Comical Hiroshi eating to his heart's content.
Relatable moments for working professionals.
Uplifting message about food and recalibration.
Cute animation, nice opening song and soundtrack.

anime.title: Dead Account
anime.synopsis: Always ready for a fight! Destruction for destruction's sake! The online streamer Aoringo is a troll, making the worst of the worst of boundary-pushing flamebait content and raking in the revenue from the hate-watchers. You may think he's nothing more than a bottom feeder and a drain on society, but in reality, he's high school dropout Souji Enishiro, a caring older brother with a sweet tooth who loves nothing more than his little sister. His viral videos? Just a way to pay his sister's medical bills. And even if all of humanity hates him, he doesn't care, so long as his little sister gets better. But then, something very strange begins to happen...  Don't miss the debut of this modern-day occult exorcism battle manga!
anime.consensus_summary: Dead Account presents a fresh take on the exorcism genre with its unique digital concept and magic system. However, it suffers from a derivative and predictable plot, along with unremarkable animation. While some appreciate its modern twist and fast pace, others find it to be a generic shonen with underdeveloped characters and a reliance on clichés, resulting in a mixed reception.
pros: Unique concept of digital exorcism
Well-developed and creative magic system based on phone usage
Fast-paced and easy-to-follow story
cons: Generic and clichéd storyline
Underdeveloped characters
Mediocre animation quality
Derivative of Jujutsu Kaisen

anime.title: Record of Ragnarok III
anime.genres: Action, Drama, Fantasy, Gore, Mythology, Seinen
anime.synopsis: Third season of Shuumatsu no Walküre.
anime.consensus_summary: Season 3 of Shuumatsu no Walküre is a mixed bag, with improvements in animation and character development offset by inconsistent visuals and repetitive storytelling. While some viewers found the fights emotionally resonant and the backstories compelling, others criticized the formulaic structure and pacing issues. Overall, the season is considered a step up from previous installments but still falls short of its potential.
pros: Improved animation quality compared to previous seasons, with impressive CGI in some fights.
Compelling character backstories, particularly for Qin Shi Huang and Beelzebub, add emotional depth.
Fights are more deliberate, with a greater sense of emotional tension and thematic weight.
cons: Inconsistent animation quality, with some scenes appearing like animated manga panels.
Formulaic fight structure with repetitive flashbacks and inner monologues disrupts pacing.
Reliance on similar soundtrack from previous seasons feels lazy and uninspired.

anime.title: Reincarnated as a Dragon Hatchling
anime.romaji_title: Tensei shitara Dragon no Tamago datta
anime.synopsis: Our hero wakes up one day in a brand new world…but his new life doesn’t come with fighting skills or magic powers, or even arms and legs! He’s reborn as a helpless egg, stuck in an unfamiliar forest surrounded by terrifying, hungry beasts. But eggs hatch, hatchlings grow up, and humble beginnings can lead to something great. He’ll do his best to become the strongest dragon ever, and no measly shell will get in his way!
anime.consensus_summary: Audience sentiment is mixed, with many finding the anime to be a passable but ultimately unfulfilling isekai. While the concept of a dragon evolving through RPG-like elements is appealing, the poor pacing, low-budget animation, and generic plot are significant drawbacks. Many feel the anime fails to live up to its potential and is easily forgettable, with some recommending the manga instead.
pros: Interesting concept of evolving dragon
Enjoyable skill system and RPG elements
Likeable side characters with human logic
cons: Poor pacing with drawn-out episodes and recaps
Mediocre animation quality with heavy CGI
Formulaic plot and uninspired villain
Generic and forgettable music
Protagonist's naivete and stupidity
Unsatisfying ending

anime.title: Inexpressive Kashiwada and Expressive Oota
anime.romaji_title: Kao ni Denai Kashiwada-san to Kao ni Deru Oota-kun
anime.synopsis:
With a smirk, Oota disregards his single-digit test scores and searches for a new source of amusement. He is soon captivated by his classmate Kashiwada, a mysterious student who consistently wears a blank face. Oota conspires to break her placid demeanor through scares and mischievous schemes, though his tactics always seem to backfire.

Oota is known as the class clown and is constantly disciplined by his teacher, who claims "his face gives it away." To no fault of his own, he lacks control of his emotions and facial expressions. Kashiwada, on the other hand, seems perpetually emotionless and unreadable—no one knows what she is thinking!

Oota and Kashiwada are complete opposites, but that does not stop a unique relationship from developing between them. As they realize their feelings for each other, it raises an important question: do opposites really attract?
anime.consensus_summary: The audience generally finds the anime cute and enjoyable, appreciating the dynamic between the main characters. However, some find the story repetitive and slow-paced, with limited plot progression. Overall, it's considered a pleasant but not particularly outstanding romantic comedy.
pros: Charming dynamic between the leads
Light-hearted and relaxing
Unique premise with opposites attracting
cons: Repetitive story format
Slow pace, minimal plot progression
Humor is not consistently strong

anime.title: Tune In to the Midnight Heart
anime.synopsis:
Back in middle school, Arisu Yamabuki's only solace in life was a radio show hosted by a girl named Apollo. He used to faithfully tune into the program every night until she abruptly stopped broadcasting entirely. Despite having very few clues about Apollo's identity, Yamabuki has thoroughly investigated her, which eventually led him to enroll in the newly co-ed Furin High School, hoping to find her there.

Just as Yamabuki suspected, the broadcasting club's first announcement is made by the familiar voice he admires! Upon entering the club room, however, Yamabuki realizes that his search will not be that easy. The four members—Rikka Inohana, Shinobu Uzuki, Nene Himekawa, and Iko Kirino—all sound like Apollo in different ways.

Yamabuki joins the club primarily to find Apollo, but he soon discovers that each girl aspires to pursue her own career with her voice. Seeing that there is a lot of room for improvement, Yamabuki takes it upon himself to help the girls reach their individual goals—but he never stops looking for his favorite Apollo.
anime.consensus_summary: Audience opinion is split, with many enjoying the story, characters, and humor, particularly the unique protagonist. However, the poor animation quality is a major point of criticism, overshadowing the positive aspects for some viewers. Manga readers are often disappointed by the adaptation's shortcomings in visual expression.
pros: Refreshing protagonist with unique personality and humor
Enjoyable character interactions and dynamics
Good voice acting and sound direction
Story explores voice-driven media in a modern and emotionally resonant way
cons: Inconsistent and often poor animation quality
Stiff character movements and off-model designs
Pacing feels rushed, hindering character development
Tries to balance too many elements (romance, comedy, mystery) without focus
Some scenes cut or reshuffled from the manga
Lack of detailed emotional expression in animation

anime.title: Scum of the Brave
anime.synopsis:
Tokyo's criminal underworld has been using medical procedures known as ether augmentation to increase their own powers and influence. To counteract this threat, bounty hunters called Braves have emerged, using their own ether powers to eliminate the powerful mafiosos known as Dark Lords. Although he is a self-proclaimed first-rate Brave, Yashiro struggles to make ends meet.

One day, Yashiro helps out a young student of Shibuya's Brave Academy named Aki Jougamine. Impressed by his skill, Aki begs him to help save her friend and fellow student, Saera Kashiwagi Pendragon, from the clutches of a Dark Lord, which he reluctantly agrees to.

After assisting them, Aki, Saera, and their friend Yukine Indou insist on apprenticing with Yashiro. Despite his attempts to dissuade them from the dangers of bounty hunting, the trio believes that Yashiro is their key to becoming full-fledged Braves, leaving him to reluctantly give in. With each new threat they encounter, Yashiro will try to convince them that the three students are not cut out for bounty hunting, but they may just prove him wrong.
anime.consensus_summary: Audience reception is divided due to significant production limitations, particularly animation quality, which overshadows a strong narrative and compelling character work. While many praise the refreshing themes and character dynamics, detractors point to plot inconsistencies and a lack of depth in the magic system and protagonist's development. Despite flaws, the show is considered a worthwhile, albeit flawed, watch by many.
pros: Engaging story with strong character development, especially for the students.
Compelling character interactions and dynamics, particularly the mentor-student relationships.
Refreshing take on the 'hero' trope with a cynical yet ultimately hopeful outlook.
Interesting use of powers and solid fight choreography despite animation limitations.
Well-written characters, even side characters are memorable or interesting.
Satisfying closed ending with good pacing for the most part.
Solid world-building that effectively integrates the power system.
cons: Noticeably low production values and cheap animation, which can be a deal-breaker.
Inconsistent or nonsensical storytelling decisions and plot holes.
Soft magic system lacks consistency and can feel like a writing convenience.
Protagonist's character development feels inconsistent or lacking in later stages.
Some character quirks become tiresome due to repetition.
Dialogue can be cheesy or cringe, and comedy relies on overused gags.
Inner monologues can be exhausting.
The show feels like 'empty calories' with a lack of memorable details after watching.

anime.title: Cute High Earth Defense Club Love!
anime.genres: Comedy, Fantasy, Historical, Parody, School, Super Power
anime.synopsis:
It's the Taisho era—a time filled with the scent of romance, and people's hearts are still filled with compassion.

Unzen, Sukayu, Unohana, Oshamanbe, and Aso are all ordinary (?) male students at Binan High School, who spend their days lazing around in the clubroom of the "do-nothing club" Earth Defense Club, and live together in the Kurotama dormitory.

One day, while the five are taking a morning bath at the Kurotama dormitory, they notice something slimy moving in the bathtub. When they finally manage to catch it, it turns out to be a talking Pallas's cat named Nuru!

Nuru has come from the distant future with a serious mission to inform them that the Earth is facing an impending threat of destruction. While he says he wants to protect the Earth, he says he's only come to warn them of the crisis, and that it's up to the five of them to decide whether or not they want to fight for the Earth...

Isn't this just an attempt to dodge responsibility? The Defense Club members are suspicious. "If either is fine with you, I'll do it! That's more fashionable!" Unzen enthusiastically says. The five decide to fight with free will, and Nuru transforms them into the Haikara Romantic Troupe using feline science.

Meanwhile, a mysterious trio called the Bankara New Elite Squad are scheming in the shadows. They are plotting to take over the Earth.
anime.consensus_summary: The audience views 'Binan Koukou Chikyuu Bouei-bu Haikara!' as a unique and enjoyable parody. Viewers appreciate its distinctive style. While some may initially dismiss it, deeper engagement reveals its brilliance.
pros: Unique and self-aware parody of magical boy genre.
Embraces a 'Haikara!' aesthetic, contributing to its charm.
cons: Initial impression might be of a simple brainrot show.
Themes may not be immediately apparent to all viewers.

anime.title: Though I Am an Inept Villainess
anime.romaji_title: Futsutsuka na Akujo dewa Gozaimasu ga: Suuguu Chouso Torikae Den
anime.synopsis:
Within the Kingdom of Ei's opulent inner court is the thriving Maiden Court, where the empress and the four imperial consorts are chosen from five prominent clans. Among them, one pristine consort-in-training, Reirin Kou, stands out as the perfect candidate for the future empress. Her virtue and elegance are unrivaled, and she is flawless—save for her extremely sickly constitution. Compared to the court's gentle butterfly, the boorish Keigetsu Shu is like a sewer rat. Always staring at Reirin with bitter envy, Keigetsu is a disgrace to the Maiden Court.

During the night of a rare comet sighting, Keigetsu's jealousy reaches its peak, and she attempts to murder Reirin by pushing her off a balcony. Reirin is quickly saved from death, and Keigetsu is imprisoned to await her execution. Unbeknownst to all, Keigetsu has cast a spell to swap bodies with Reirin in order to steal all that belongs to her. But while Keigetsu is hindered by Reirin's frail body, Reirin fully embraces freedom and physical strength for the first time in her life, determined to live—no matter whose face she wears.
anime.consensus_summary: The audience is largely positive, praising the anime for its stunning visuals, engaging plot, and compelling characters, especially its unique take on the body-swap trope. However, a segment of the audience finds the main protagonist to be overly perfect, bordering on a 'Mary Sue,' which detracts from the narrative for some viewers.
pros: Visually stunning with high attention to detail in art, character designs, and costumes.
Engaging and well-crafted plot with an intriguing body-swap premise used effectively.
Strong character development and compelling interpersonal relationships.
Addictive and charming atmosphere, praised for its addictive nature.
Excellent voice acting performances that sell the dual roles effectively.
Inspiring protagonist who finds opportunities amidst adversity.
Fresh take on established tropes, offering a unique feel compared to other seasonal anime.
cons: Protagonist can be perceived as too perfect or a 'Mary Sue' with a lack of noticeable flaws.
Some supporting characters can fall into predictable patterns.
Limited worldbuilding outside the palace, making the surrounding world feel flat.
Repetitive character introductions with on-screen nametags can feel condescending to the audience.
Story and characters could benefit from more depth.

anime.title: Digimon Beatbreak
anime.synopsis:
Tomorou Tenma possesses a uniquely strong e-Pulse—the energy created by human thoughts and emotions that powers egg-shaped AI devices named Sapotama. The world's everyday life relies on the assistance of Sapotamas, but the force of Tomorou's e-Pulse often causes glitches in them. One night, a strange creature calling itself Gekkoumon emerges from his device and insists on eating Tomorou's e-Pulse.

Gekkoumon is a Digimon, a creature feeding on e-Pulse that was born from an error in Sapotamas. Some Digimon completely drain humans of their energy, leaving them in a comatose state known as Cold Heart. When Tomorou's older brother, Asuka, becomes a victim of this phenomenon, Tomorou vows to avenge him.

Tomorou meets a group of Digimon-wielders called Glowing Dawn, who hunt down rogue Digimon for bounties. Their leader, Kyou Sawashiro, explains that there might still be hope for Asuka's recovery. Although Tomorou struggles to trust these strangers, he decides to join them, as he realizes that saving his brother may not be achievable on his own.
anime.consensus_summary: Audience reception is largely positive, with strong praise for its mature themes, cyberpunk setting, and character development. However, some viewers find the early pacing slow and the animation inconsistent, leading to mild disagreement on core elements. It's seen as a significant evolution for the franchise, appealing to older fans and newcomers willing to engage with a more serious narrative.
pros: Mature themes and complex narratives suitable for an older audience.
Strong world-building and detailed cyberpunk/dystopian setting.
Character development and interpersonal relationships are well-handled.
Explores relevant societal anxieties like AI reliance and social inequality.
Engaging plot progression, moving away from episodic structures of previous seasons.
cons: Animation quality is described as serviceable or uneven at times.
Pacing in the early episodes can be slow or episodic, requiring patience.
Some character motivations (e.g., Kyo's) can feel clichéd or disappointing.
Digivolution moments can lack emotional impact or buildup.
Dialogue can sometimes feel formulaic or rely on catchphrases.

anime.title: Milky☆Subway: The Galactic Limited Express
anime.synopsis:
Arrested for reckless space driving, super human Chiharu and cyborg Makina are sentenced to clean the Milky☆Subway—an old interplanetary train.

Easy enough, right? Wrong. When the train suddenly takes off, they are thrown into a high-speed space-train spectacle packed with chaos, no plans, and zero strategy.

Just pure momentum!
anime.consensus_summary: Audiences generally find Ginga Tokkyuu Milky☆Subway to be a fun and entertaining short anime. The animation, voice acting, and comedic timing are highly praised, especially considering the limited runtime. Some viewers desire more depth and longer episodes, but overall, the show is well-received for its lighthearted and engaging nature.
pros: Excellent voice acting in both Japanese and English dubs.
Impressive 3D animation quality, especially facial expressions.
Sharp comic timing and effective use of short runtime.
Charismatic characters with great chemistry.
Snappy dialogue and distinct aesthetic.
cons: Short runtime leaves the audience wanting more.
Some scenes are chaotic due to characters talking over each other.
Lacks overall depth to elevate it from good to fantastic.
The plot is minimalistic.

anime.title: The Banished Court Magician Aims to Become the Strongest
anime.romaji_title: Mikata ga Yowasugite Hojo Mahou ni Tesshiteita Kyuutei Mahoushi, Tsuihou sarete Saikyou wo Mezasu
anime.synopsis:
"This party doesn't need an incompetent magician who can only use supportive magic. You're fired, Alec Ygret."

Suddenly, Alec, a court magician who had joined the crown prince's party to help him conquer dungeons—was banished from the party. And not just the party, but the crown prince's harassment has banished him from the royal palace as well, and a friend from the "magic academy" approached Alec, who was at his wit's end.

"Hey, Alec. Do you want to try to conquer the dungeon with us again?"

And so, together with the friends he used to party with, Alec begins his second journey in life. This is the adventure story of a former court magician who had been abandoned.

Four years ago, the "Lasting Period," a party of four that had been called "legendary," has gradually spread its name around the world.
anime.consensus_summary: The anime is viewed as a generic isekai with a familiar 'banished' plot. While some enjoy the character interactions and easy-to-watch nature, many find the story bland, the main character uninspired, and the world-building lacking. The series doesn't stand out in a crowded genre, leading to a generally lukewarm reception.
pros: Decent characters with good interactions.
Enjoyable, easy-to-watch storyline.
Some interesting world-building elements.
The main party members are all skilled and have established relationships.
cons: Generic plot with overused 'banished' trope.
Lack of meaningful world-building and complex story.
Bland main character with little motivation or personality.
Inconsistent power scaling and plot holes.
Story feels like an allegory and lacks focus on fantasy elements.

anime.title: Draw This, Then Die!
anime.synopsis:
Ai Yasumi, a first-year high school student living on Izu-Oshima, loves manga more than anything. When she learns that her long-admired, yet long-inactive, favorite manga artist Hoshi no Rei will be exhibiting at COMITIA, she sets off on a journey to Tokyo.

What she doesn't expect, however, is that a fateful encounter at the event will change her life forever.

"How does one become a manga artist?" Ai steps into the world of manga creation—a path she thought she understood, yet knows so little about. This is the story of a girl taking her first steps down the road to becoming a mangaka.
anime.consensus_summary: The audience overwhelmingly loves Kore Kaite Shine, praising its heartfelt exploration of creativity, the manga industry, and character relationships. While a few minor criticisms exist regarding tropiness and standard animation, the overall sentiment is highly positive, with many considering it a standout series.
pros: The anime effectively contrasts the pure joy of discovering manga with the brutal realities of pursuing art, creating a grounded and emotionally resonant story.

The character development, particularly the dynamic between the protagonist and her teacher, is highlighted as a strong point, with reviewers appreciating the exploration of their pasts and inner thoughts.
The production quality, including art direction, character animation, and background visuals, is praised, with special mention of how manga scenes are depicted.
The narrative successfully captures the passion and soul of manga creation while also being relatable and earnest in a universal way.
cons: Some reviewers found the show to be tropy at times, particularly within the CGDCT (Cute Girls Doing Cute Things) elements, which detracted from their enjoyment.
The absence of the protagonist's parents in the early episodes was noted as a minor issue, potentially missing an opportunity to reinforce themes.
While animation is generally solid, some noted it was standard and not exceptionally high-quality, with a few wishing for more 'Sakuga' moments.

anime.title: Mobile Suit Gundam GQuuuuuuX -Beginning-
anime.synopsis:
Amate Yuzuriha is a high-school student living peacefully in a space colony floating in outer space. When she meets a war refugee named Nyaan, Amate is drawn into the illegal mobile suit dueling sport known as Clan Battle.

Under the entry name "Machu," she throws herself into fierce battle day after day, piloting the GQuuuuuuX. Then an unidentified Gundam mobile suit pursued by both the space force and the police appears before her, along with its pilot, a boy named Shuji.
anime.consensus_summary: Audience members show interest in the alternative timeline and callbacks to the original series, but concerns arise regarding character development, voice acting, and reliance on tropes and plot elements from other anime series like Evangelion and Utena. There is cautious optimism for the TV series version, but concerns remain about repeating mistakes from previous Gundam series like Witch From Mercury.
pros: Excitement for an alternative timeline where Char pilots the RX78.
Callbacks to the original 0079 series are appreciated.
Amate's character shows potential for development.
cons: Char's new voice actor is considered flat.
The series borrows too heavily from Evangelion and Utena.
Concerns that the Clan Battle concept, similar to WFM, may not work well.
anime.thematic_vibe: Alternative Timeline, Mobile Suit Battles, High School Drama

anime.title: Re:ZERO -Starting Life in Another World- Season 4
anime.romaji_title: Re:Zero kara Hajimeru Isekai Seikatsu 4th Season
anime.genres: Drama, Fantasy, Isekai, Psychological, Suspense, Time Travel
anime.synopsis: In the deadly battle at the Watergate City of Priestella, Subaru and his allies barely emerged victorious—but their triumph came at a great cost. Through the "Authority of Gluttony," Rem was put into suspended animation, while Crusch's memories and even Julius’s name were devoured. As he searches for a way to save them, Subaru learns of the "Sage" Shaula—an all-seeing being said to possess every form of knowledge. His next destination is the Pleiades Watchtower, home to the Sage, the farthest tower standing in the vast, uncharted desert known as the Auguria Dunes—a place so perilous that even the mightiest "Sword Saint," Reinhard, failed to conquer it. The fury of nature, unknown magical beasts, and unimaginable dangers lie ahead. Together with his friends, Subaru embarks on a life-risking journey to reclaim what was lost.
anime.consensus_summary: Audience opinion is sharply divided, with many viewers feeling the series has become repetitive, over-reliant on its core gimmick, and has lost the narrative focus that made earlier seasons compelling. Conversely, a significant portion of the audience still finds the series to be a masterful example of the isekai genre, praising its emotional depth, character development, and production values, particularly in the latest season.
pros: Animation quality is a solid 8/10, but it can't carry the series for me.
Animation is beautiful, direction grabs all your attention.
OST and background music genuinely elevate so many moments.
The direction was perfect here, as the confined space, the sound design and fast pacing made this scene feel as if some evil force was suffocating them.
The voice acting is great
The production is good
The staff has really put their all into making sure they deliver this story the best it could possibly be.
cons: The show is just plain bad; the main character is always screaming, and the plot feels spotty.
Compression issues from translating the light novel into a few anime episodes, and it is quite noticeable.
None of the characters tie the viewer to the show anymore; they all fall flat with barely any redeeming qualities.
It has become repetitive. Certain plotlines and emotional beats feel recycled, just with different characters attached to them.
The narrative structure of Season 4 remains trapped in the same exhausting, manipulative loop that has plagued the series from day one.
The central gimmick, the Return by Death ability, completely destroys any actual stakes.
Calling it the "greatest isekai" and acting like its a high bar to clear really doesnt add much to the conversation considering it is no better than the isekais it claims to be "better than".
The character designs themselves are not just aesthetically bad, they feel actively predatory.
Subaru's unlikable character at the start was a tough watch, in a good way, and felt like a genuine look at some relatively relatable character flaws.
His development hits a wall in season 3.
The main heroine, Emilia, is pretty bland.
The anime dialogues feels really cringe but the BIGGEST problem the MC, he just depends on every one else and other characters give all of their achievements credit to him
The story constantly tries to have its cake and eat it too.

anime.title: Dr. Stone: Science Future Part 2
anime.synopsis:
After a strategic maneuver, Senkuu Ishigami's team stalls Dr. Xeno's more scientifically advanced forces. A ceasefire between the two factions allows for the establishment of Corn City in North America, a hope for a future thriving population. Meanwhile, Senkuu and some of his teammates rush toward the Amazon in South America—the epicenter of the petrification beam's impact—to create Superalloy City and progress their spaceship project.

With dangerous enemies still pursuing Senkuu and his companions, it is a race against time to reach the heart of the dense Amazon. As unexpected allies and scientific creations further fuel this leg of their journey, Senkuu is closer than ever to finally uncovering the mystery behind the petrification phenomenon.
anime.consensus_summary: Audience reception is mixed, with some praising the season's evolution, tension, and character development, while others criticize the declining writing quality, erosion of the science aspect, and convoluted plot. There's a clear divide between those who appreciate the high-stakes adventure and those who feel the series has strayed too far from its original strengths. While many find the season enjoyable, there are significant concerns about the direction of the narrative and its reliance on 'rule of cool' plot twists.
pros: Evolution of initial premise well executed
Introduction of formidable adversaries equal to Senku
Improved pacing and tension
Character growth and depth
Balance of adventure, comedy, and emotion
cons: Decline in writing quality
Science aspect nearly erased
Convoluted story and confusing truce conditions
Pacing drags in build-up episodes

anime.title: Anyway, I'm Falling in Love with You. Season 2
anime.genres: Drama, Reverse Harem, Romance, School, Shoujo
anime.synopsis:
As seasons have passed, Mizuho Nishino's adolescence has been full of ups and downs. With Christmas approaching, she intends to celebrate the special event with all of her four childhood friends: Kizuki Hazawa, Shin Kashiwagi, Airu Izumi, and Shuugo Hoshikawa. However, Kizuki makes the first move when he declares that he wants to spend the time alone with Mizuho. Although hesitant at first, Mizuho ends up confiding in him and declares Kizuki to be her boyfriend!

The news about Mizuho and Kizuki spreads quickly and brings forth Shin and Airu, who have had a difficult time accepting their feelings for the one they love. With the friend group faced with a delicate situation they have never confronted before, only time will tell if the new romance and old friendships can survive.
anime.consensus_summary: The second season of 'Douse, Koishite Shimaunda' is largely considered a disappointment. Critics highlight a confusing plot, frustrating character decisions, and uninspired animation. While some find nostalgic value or enjoy the side stories, the consensus leans heavily negative, with many regretting giving the series a second chance.
pros: Some viewers find the side character stories (Airu and Shugo) to be enjoyable.
The anime evokes nostalgic feelings in some viewers, reminding them of their high school experiences.
cons: The plot is confusing and jumps between past and present without warning.
The drama feels forced and unnecessary, often resolved quickly without consequences.
Character choices are baffling and frustrating, particularly Kizuki's actions.
The main character, Mizuho, lacks personality and agency.
The animation is simplistic and visually unappealing, with poor background design and a bright filter.
The story's ending feels predictable and negates the impact of previous events.
The interactions are perceived as cheesy

anime.title: Blue Miburo Season 2
anime.synopsis: Second season of Ao no Miburo.
anime.consensus_summary: The second season is considered a significant improvement over the first, with praise for its character development, dramatic storytelling, and adherence to historical events. Viewers appreciate the exploration of internal conflicts and the emotional depth of the characters. While some minor criticisms exist regarding reused music, the overall sentiment is positive, particularly among fans of historical dramas and samurai themes.
pros: Improved character development compared to the first season.
Tasteful portrayal of tragedy.
Solid animation and music create a proper atmosphere.
Exploration of characters' fears and anxieties.
Faithful to historical content.
cons: Some noticeable music tracks reused from the first season.

anime.title: Medalist Season 2
anime.synopsis:
Ever since the novice coach Tsukasa Akeuraji took Inori Yuitsuka under his mentorship, she has improved her figure skating at a fast pace. After passing a qualifying badge test, she earns a spot to compete in the upcoming Chubu Block Tournament, where only five of the 15 competitors can move forward to the next stage—the prestigious All-Japan Novice Tournament. However, earning a slot will not be easy for Inori: most of her rivals have already experienced trying their luck in the competition.

The stakes are high as the competition begins, and one by one, each of the competitors strive to perform their very best in front of the big crowd. Moreover, the current figure skating generation's prodigy, Hikaru Kamisaki, is not competing in this block, which raises everyone's determination to qualify. That includes Inori, who must beat the odds if she wants to keep her promise to reach Hikaru and represent Japan in the Olympics with Tsukasa.
anime.consensus_summary: The second season of Medalist is generally well-received, particularly for its character development and animation quality. However, some viewers feel that the season is rushed and serves primarily as a setup for the upcoming movie. While the core elements are praised, there are criticisms regarding pacing, limited character development for supporting characters, and occasional inconsistencies in visual quality, leading to mild disagreement.
pros: Strong character development, especially for Inori and Tsukasa
High-quality animation, particularly the blending of CGI with 2D drawings in skating sequences
Engaging story with a focus on internal struggles and personal growth
Effective portrayal of the coach-skater relationship
Detailed and comprehensible explanations of figure skating techniques and strategies
cons: Rushed pacing due to the short 9-episode season
Limited development for new and returning supporting characters
Over-reliance on familiar narrative formula, lacking innovation
Inconsistent visual quality, with occasional awkward compositing and CG assets
Transitional season focused on setting up the movie, leading to a lack of a satisfying finale

anime.title: Toilet-Bound Hanako-kun Season 2 Part 2
anime.synopsis:
Due to frequent misadventures with the supernatural and her hectic school life, Nene Yashiro can barely catch a break until Kamome Academy's annual sleepover event comes around. Nene is excited to blow off some steam with her best friend Aoi Akane and the rest of her class at the get-together. Unbeknownst to her, the sleepover falls on the same date as Urabon, when the line between the dead and the living gets distorted, allowing wicked spirits to come out to the surface.

When an evil ghost is about to attack her, Nene is rescued by a mysterious figure: Shinigami, the Sixth Wonder that can trap souls using his flute. In that moment, Shinigami takes notice of Aoi and abducts her to use her as a sacrifice that will close the barrier for good. Joined by Hanako-kun and Akane Aoi, Nene must embark on a journey into the deepest confines of the world of the dead to save her best friend before it is too late.
anime.consensus_summary: The audience generally loves 'Jibaku Shounen Hanako-kun 2 Part 2,' praising its visuals, manga faithfulness, and emotional depth. Some find it less compelling than previous installments, particularly in terms of plot engagement. The strong fanbase appreciates the romantic development, but some feel it might overshadow other elements.
pros: Stunning art style and animation
Faithful manga adaptation
Emotional and tear-jerking plot
Good opening song
cons: Pacing and story engagement weaker than previous seasons (Part 1 of Season 2)
Not enough manga content for another season yet
Potentially too focused on romance for some viewers

anime.title: You Can't Be In a Rom-Com with Your Childhood Friends!
anime.romaji_title: Osananajimi to wa Love Comedy ni Naranai
anime.synopsis:
As a romantic comedy enthusiast, Yonosuke "Eiyuu" Sakai enjoys the stories about childhood friends the most. But he solemnly believes that the flawless, loving childhood friends from his stories exist only in fiction. Though he has two childhood friends of his own—Shio Minamo and Akari Hiodoshi—Eiyuu has never seen either one of them as anything more.

However, now that they are all in high school together, the beauty of the two girls begins to catch Eiyuu's eye. As his interest subtly grows, the girls start to make advances toward him regardless of time or place—but only time will tell if Eiyuu will ever overcome his denial and finally see the girls in another light.
anime.consensus_summary: Audience reception is mixed, with some finding enjoyment in the series' comedic and ecchi elements, while others are frustrated by the dense main character, lack of plot progression, and reliance on overused tropes. The show is considered a generic harem rom-com, with some viewers finding it entertaining as a time-waster, while others find it boring and repetitive. The ending is widely criticized for resolving nothing and leaving the story stagnant.
pros: Catchy opening theme and generally well-received OST/SFX
Some found the series enjoyable as a lighthearted comedy with ecchi elements
Several reviewers highlighted individual characters (particularly Shio and Haru) as being enjoyable and carrying the show
cons: Frustratingly dense main character and stagnant plot with no character development
Over-reliance on rom-com tropes and repetitive scenarios
Lack of meaningful progress in the relationships between characters
Mediocre animation quality mentioned
Ending that resolves nothing and leaves the story in the same status quo
anime.thematic_vibe: Harem, Romantic Comedy, Slice of Life

anime.title: Ancient War Soul
anime.genres: Action, Adventure, Fantasy, Historical, Martial Arts, Reincarnation
anime.synopsis: A generation of martial arts emperor was killed and fell, and ten thousand years later he was reborn in a young man named Qin Feng. He awakened the supreme spirit and practiced the supreme martial arts. From then on, he fought against countless geniuses. All the heavens and the worlds will tremble because of his return!
anime.consensus_summary: The donghua has good technical aspects such as animation and world-building, but is ultimately let down by a predictable and unoriginal story with annoying and hollow characters.  The generic plot and poor character development overshadow the positive aspects, leading to a disappointing viewing experience. It is unlikely to be enjoyed by those familiar with higher-quality donghua.
pros: Decent animation quality
Good setting and artistic quality
Decent world-building
Decent action scenes
cons: Simple and annoying plot
Predictable cultivation genre
Unoriginal story
Annoying and insignificant characters
Hollow characters
Poor characterization

anime.title: The Klutzy Class Monitor and the Girl with the Short Skirt
anime.romaji_title: Ponkotsu Fuuki Iin to Skirt-take ga Futekisetsu na JK no Hanashi
anime.synopsis:
Sakuradaimon takes his role on the school's Public Morals Committee very seriously. Every day, he dutifully checks students' appearances at the school gate—most often scolding Kohinata, a rule-breaking girl with bright hair and a short skirt.

Though she finds his constant lecturing annoying, everything changes when she discovers that Sakuradaimon is actually a bit of a mess himself.

A lighthearted short romantic comedy about a strict committee member, a bold classmate, and the chaotic school life that brings them together.
anime.consensus_summary: The audience generally regards "Ponkotsu Fuuki Iin to Skirt-take ga Futekisetsu na JK no Hanashi" as a highly enjoyable and funny rom-com with a unique art style and strong lead chemistry. While most praise its wholesome nature and humor, some critique its pacing and a lack of focus on the main couple in the latter half of the season.
pros: Strong chemistry and natural progression between the main couple
Genuinely funny comedy that lands consistently
Unique and eye-catching art style and animation
Well-developed and charming supporting cast
Wholesome and heartwarming tone, avoiding excessive fanservice
cons: Pacing issues, particularly in the second half
Lack of focus on the main couple after introducing side characters
Underdeveloped plotlines for side characters
Ambiguous identity regarding whether it's a comedy or slice-of-life
Some criticized the repetitive jokes and the finale's execution

anime.title: Agents of the Four Seasons: Dance of Spring
anime.synopsis:
For centuries, the task of bringing the seasons has been carried out by the Agents of the Four Seasons, individuals whose god-like powers make them an easy target for covetous groups. One such group, the Rebels, orchestrates an attack on the Agents. To save the others, the Agent of Spring, Hinagiku Kayou, allows herself to be captured and disappears from the face of the Earth. Despite the lack of help, even from her own village, Hinagiku's guard, Sakura Himedaka, believes she is still alive somewhere and refuses to give up the search.

Against all odds, Hinagiku is found 10 years later. However, the traumatic event caused a massive shift in her personality. Thanks to Sakura's encouragement, Hinagiku gets the courage to summon the season that was once lost. In order to move forward, the duo must face a past that haunts them and demons willing to destroy everything to achieve their goals.
anime.consensus_summary: Audience reception is deeply divided, with strong praise for its stunning animation, unique world-building, and sensitive exploration of trauma, contrasted by significant criticism of its inconsistent pacing, tonal clashes, and underdeveloped plot elements. While some found it deeply moving and artistically brilliant, others felt it was melodramatic, poorly paced, and failed to live up to its narrative potential.
pros: Stunning animation and production values, particularly the visual direction and art style.
Exploration of deep psychological themes, especially trauma and identity, handled with sensitivity by some.
Unique and well-crafted world-building around the concept of the Four Seasons Agents.
Strong emotional moments and character relationships, particularly between the Agents and their Guards.
cons: Inconsistent pacing, with significant portions feeling like filler or slow plot progression.
Jarring tonal shifts between heavy drama and jarring action/espionage elements.
Antagonistic forces and their motivations are often poorly explained or underdeveloped.
Some character arcs feel underdeveloped or end unsatisfactorily, with a perceived lack of closure.
Overreliance on music and visuals to convey emotion, sometimes at the expense of earned narrative development.

anime.title: Steel Ball Run: JoJo's Bizarre Adventure
anime.romaji_title: Steel Ball Run: JoJo no Kimyou na Bouken
anime.genres: Action, Adventure, Historical, Mystery, Racing, Seinen, Shounen, Supernatural
anime.synopsis:
In the American Old West, the world's greatest race is about to begin. Thousands line up in San Diego to travel over six thousand kilometers for a chance to win the grand prize of fifty million dollars. With the era of the horse reaching its end, contestants are allowed to use any kind of vehicle they wish. Competitors will have to endure grueling conditions, traveling up to a hundred kilometers a day through uncharted wastelands. The Steel Ball Run is truly a one-of-a-kind event.

The youthful Johnny Joestar, a crippled former horse racer, has come to San Diego to watch the start of the race. There he encounters Gyro Zeppeli, a racer with two steel balls at his waist instead of a gun. Johnny witnesses Gyro using one of his steel balls to unleash a fantastical power, compelling a man to fire his gun at himself during a duel. In the midst of the action, Johnny happens to touch the steel ball and feels a power surging through his legs, allowing him to stand up for the first time in two years. Vowing to find the secret of the steel balls, Johnny decides to compete in the race, and so begins his bizarre adventure across America on the Steel Ball Run.
anime.consensus_summary: Audience opinion is sharply divided, primarily between those deeply disappointed by the anime adaptation's perceived failures in animation and pacing, and those who, despite acknowledging flaws, still find enjoyment due to the strength of the source material. There is near-universal agreement that the manga is superior, leading to significant frustration over the perceived mishandling of the adaptation, particularly concerning the animation quality and the ending's music.
pros: The source material (manga) is widely praised and considered great.
The core story, character dynamics (Johnny and Gyro), and unique concept are strong.
Voice acting and sound design are generally considered good.
Some reviewers note moments of "hype" and impressive CGI during racing sequences.
The shift to a Western setting and epic scale is seen as fresh by some.
cons: The anime adaptation is widely considered disappointing and lackluster compared to the manga.
Animation quality is heavily criticized as inconsistent, lazy, clunky, and a step down from previous JoJo adaptations.
Pacing issues are noted, with scenes being cut or rushed, negatively impacting character development and relationships (especially Johnny and Gyro's).
The opening and especially the ending music/outro are frequently and intensely disliked.
Character designs and art style in the anime are seen as a downgrade from the manga.
The adaptation is perceived as not faithful to the manga, prioritizing hype over narrative substance.

anime.title: Jaadugar: A Witch in Mongolia
anime.synopsis: Eight centuries ago, in the latter days of the Islamic golden age, a young girl arrived in the Khwarazmian city of Tus. She was a slave. But she learned. Eight centuries ago, the Mongols blazed across the map, swept Khwarazm into the ash heap of history, and took all they desired from the ruins. They took the girl who learned. So begins the true story of how a "witch," wielding knowledge as her only weapon, came to hold the greatest empire the world has ever known in the palm of her hand...
anime.consensus_summary: Tenmaku no Jaadugar has garnered significant praise for its stunning historical accuracy, compelling character development, and high production quality. While the deliberate pacing and certain narrative choices have drawn minor criticism, the overwhelming sentiment is one of awe and deep engagement with its unique and thought-provoking story. Audiences widely appreciate its respectful portrayal of diverse cultures and its departure from typical anime tropes.
pros: Stunning and historically accurate depiction of 13th-century Persian and Mongolian cultures, including architecture, clothing, food, traditions, and spirituality.
Magnificent storytelling that feels like watching a feature-length film, with excellent pacing and engaging characters.
Deeply empathetic and relatable protagonist whose journey of growth and resilience is a strong emotional anchor.
Exceptional character writing that avoids common anime tropes, presenting believable and complex individuals with nuanced motivations.
Beautiful and unique art style that brings the era to life, with expressive facial animations and vibrant backgrounds.
High-quality production values, including animation, voice acting, and a soundtrack that blends Middle Eastern and Central Asian influences.
Thought-provoking narrative that explores themes of revenge, identity, and the ambiguity of good and evil, challenging viewer perspectives.
cons: The deliberate, slow pacing may be too slow for viewers seeking fast-paced action.
Some viewers may find the protagonist's internal monologues and motivations difficult to empathize with or believe.
The ending of the season was described by one reviewer as melodramatic and disappointing, failing to support the visuals.
The show's historical fiction nature, while appreciated by many, might be a point of contention for those seeking strict factual accuracy.

anime.title: Mistress Kanan is Devilishly Easy
anime.genres: Comedy, Ecchi, Romance, School, Shounen, Supernatural
anime.synopsis:
Kanan is a demon who descends upon the human world with one goal: to feast on the sweetest delicacy of all—young human souls. Disguised as a high schooler, she sets her sights on her first target, an unassuming boy named Youji Kyougi. But just as she prepares to claim her meal, things take a very unexpected turn.

Instead of devouring him, Kanan ends up forming a "romantic contract" with Youji. For someone who's lived for millennia without experiencing love, navigating high school romance proves more terrifying than any hunt. Between awkward dates, hand-holding mishaps, and feelings she can't quite name, the once-proud demon finds herself flustered at every turn.
